financial_anchor.caveat: Treat as an unverified reported anchor until a direct H1 report supports it; transactions and tax timing make doubling non-normalized.

ai_claim.claim: Iberdrola publicly describes AI for grids and renewable operations, but a named material production cohort with outage or cash results was not verified.
ai_claim.stage: E1 public AI program/capability; no opened material deployment cohort
ai_claim.scope: Specific workflow only; infrastructure demand is separated from own productivity.
ai_claim.limitation: No representative controlled cohort or retained-cash reconciliation.

strongest_counterevidence.claim: regulated allowances may pass savings to customers.
strongest_counterevidence.limitation: Does not itself disprove the scoped mechanism.

rights_limit: Public terms do not prove universal training or pooled cross-customer reuse; enterprise schedules were unavailable.
materiality_summary: Conditional arithmetic only: if H1 reported net profit was €4.34bn, 5% × (2 × €4.34bn) = €434m after tax. The figure was not extracted from the interactive hub, and simple doubling is not normalized for transactions or tax timing. Illustrative cost assumptions produce negative €20m pre-tax and are not directly comparable.

arithmetic.inputs: pool €5bn eligible grid operations, maintenance and loss/outage cost; efficiency 8%; realization 40%; retained share 50%; recurring cost €100m
arithmetic.formula: eligible cost × efficiency × realization × retained share − recurring AI expense
